title: The app can't read its secrets after moving to managed identity
intro: The orders app on vm-app-01 was migrated from a client secret to its managed identity 'to get rid of secrets'. It now fails at startup: 'Caller is not authorized to perform action on resource ... Action: Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/getSecret/action'. The platform team insists 'we gave it Contributor on the resource group'.

steps.prompt: Get the principal id of vm-app-01's system-assigned identity (rg-web-prod).
expected_commands: az vm identity show --resource-group rg-web-prod --name vm-app-01 --query principalId
az vm identity show -g rg-web-prod -n vm-app-01 --query principalId
steps.hint: az vm identity show returns the identity's principalId.

steps.prompt: List every role assignment of principal 5e6f7a8b-9c0d-4e1f-8a2b-3c4d5e6f7a8b.
steps.hint: Use --all so assignments at every scope are shown.

steps.prompt: Contributor is a control-plane role. Check which permission model the vault kv-web-prod uses.
steps.hint: enableRbacAuthorization true means data access is decided by Azure RBAC roles, not vault access policies.

steps.prompt: The vault uses RBAC, so the identity needs a data-plane role. Assign 'Key Vault Secrets User' to 5e6f7a8b-9c0d-4e1f-8a2b-3c4d5e6f7a8b at the vault's scope /subscriptions/33333333-dddd-4eee-8fff-444444444444/resourceGroups/rg-web-prod/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/kv-web-prod.
expected_commands: az role assignment create --assignee 5e6f7a8b-9c0d-4e1f-8a2b-3c4d5e6f7a8b --role "Key Vault Secrets User" --scope /subscriptions/33333333-dddd-4eee-8fff-444444444444/resourceGroups/rg-web-prod/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/kv-web-prod

steps.prompt: Now remove the over-broad Contributor assignment from 5e6f7a8b-9c0d-4e1f-8a2b-3c4d5e6f7a8b on /subscriptions/33333333-dddd-4eee-8fff-444444444444/resourceGroups/rg-web-prod. The app never needed it.
steps.fake_output: (no output: the Contributor assignment was removed)
steps.hint: az role assignment delete with the same assignee, role, and scope.

resolution: Azure splits permissions into the control plane (manage resources: 'actions') and the data plane (use their contents: 'dataActions'). Contributor on the resource group let the VM's identity reconfigure the vault, and delete every VM in the group, but not read a single secret, because getSecret is a data action. On an RBAC-model vault that needs a data role such as Key Vault Secrets User. The error message named the exact data action, which is the clue. Removing Contributor matters as much as adding the right role: 'give it Contributor to make it work' is how an app compromise becomes a whole-environment compromise. Also expect a few minutes' delay after a role assignment; restarting the app immediately and seeing another 403 doesn't mean the fix is wrong.
